findings.requirement: Reader-visible traceability and status must reproduce the current round-7 graph state without a categorical overclaim or stale pending statement. README.md, round-7-resolution.md, and traceability §10 say regeneration is complete for the current PLAN/manifest bytes and all 28 dynamically derived headings.

review/requirements-traceability.md line 108 says: ‘The current round-7 formal edit now makes its byte digests and heading set stale pending later regeneration’.
review/requirements-traceability.md line 112 says: ‘the schema-3 material graph now matches the current PLAN/manifest digests and all 27 headings’.
The same file at lines 121 and 131 says the round-7 graph matches the current bytes and all 28 headings. README.md and review/round-7-resolution.md agree with 28 and completed regeneration.
Independent recomputation confirms the graph’s PLAN and manifest digests match current bytes and its ordered heading set equals all 28 dynamically enumerated numbered headings.
findings.impact: The sole requirements/status register gives mutually exclusive current package states. A reader can conclude that the pre-closure editorial regeneration is still blocked or that the current normative heading coverage is 27, even though the checked graph is current and covers 28. This fails the requested no-stale-pending/no-contradictory-status closure condition and leaves R7-REQ-002’s status correction incomplete.
findings.required_plan_repair: Edit traceability §§6–8 so each paragraph is explicitly historical and does not call a superseded round-6 graph current. Remove both statements that round-7 regeneration is pending/stale. Replace the ‘current ... all 27 headings’ sentence with historical round-6 wording or the current completed 28-heading status. Preserve the distinct future immutable re-fetch and human semantic-review gate.
